title: NP membership of bounded machine acceptance
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine-code scheme whose canonizer has a polynomially bounded running-time function. The language of strings that can be written as $\langle\alpha,\langle x,\langle 1^n,1^t\rangle\rangle$, where $1^m$ denotes a string of $m$ ones, and for which there is a string $u$ of length $n$ such that the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts after exactly $t$ steps on input $\langle x,u\rangle$ and outputs the single bit $1$, belongs to NP.
hypotheses_covered: The canonizer running-time function of $c$ is polynomially bounded
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective machine-code scheme whose canonizer computes the serialization
of the decoded machine, and suppose its running-time function is polynomially bounded.
Then the language of encodings of a machine description, an input, and unary bounds
$n,t$, for which some word $u$ of length $n$ makes the decoded machine halt within $t$
steps on the paired input and output $1$, belongs to NP.
